name: Layer-Minor Calculus for Replicated Repairs
statement: For a replicated repair assembly $X(\mathbf R)=(S\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_a(\{a\}\times R_a)$ and a layer coordinate $e\in E$, restriction to $e=i$ replaces every occurrence row by $\rho_e^iR_a=\{t|_{E\setminus\{e\}}:t\in R_a,t_e=i\}$, while contraction of $e$ replaces it by $\pi_eR_a=\{t|_{E\setminus\{e\}}:t\in R_a\}$. Empty rows are discarded and full rows are absorbed into the common core. The normalized images are again replicated repair assemblies with the surviving acquired-support labels $P_a$. Thus all elementary pc-minors in marked layer coordinates are computed inside the finite labelled occurrence cover. In particular, if the assembly is a forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes, all $3|E|$ normalized layer-coordinate images are dismantlable ample.
proof: A word survives the restriction $e=i$ exactly when its layer word has bit $i$ there, and suppressing the coordinate produces $\rho_e^iR_a$. Coordinate contraction is the union of the two restricted sections, hence projects each row to $\pi_eR_a$. The replicated-repair recovery theorem gives the stated normalization and preserves the surviving labels. The final assertion is the elementary-minor condition for forbidden pc-minors.
